es.text: Estar como pez en el agua
es.literal: to be like a fish in water
es.meaning: To feel completely at ease in a setting.
es.example: En una cocina profesional está como pez en el agua.
es.exampleTranslation: In a professional kitchen she's in her element.

it.literal: to be a fish out of water
it.meaning: To be out of one's element; visibly out of place.
it.example: In quella situazione ero un pesce fuor d'acqua perché non conoscevo nessuno.
it.exampleTranslation: In that situation I was a fish out of water — I didn't know anyone.

bridge.note: Same fish, opposite default. Spanish keeps it in the water and describes belonging; Italian pulls it out and describes the lack of it. Both languages can form both halves, but each reaches by habit for one — and the halves mean opposite things.

interference.es_to_it: Translating the positive straight across as 'come un pesce nell'acqua' lands as formal; Italian's live form is the negative.
interference.it_to_es: The negative does transfer — Spanish has 'como pez fuera del agua' — but it is the marked half of the pair. An Italian who only ever reaches for the negative will sound oddly bleak in Spanish.
